The vulnerability affects Axios versions prior to 0.30.3 (0.x branch) and prior to 1.13.5 (1.x branch). It was disclosed on February 8, 2026, and carries a CVSS v3.1 base score of 7.5 (High) (GitHub Advisory). Technical details The root cause is classified as CWE-754 (Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions). The flaw exists in lib/core/mergeConfig.js at lines 98–101, where Object.keys({ ...config1, ...config2 }) is iterated without filtering dangerous prototype-related keys. When __proto__ appears as an own enumerable property (as produced by JSON.parse('{ \"__proto__\": {...} }')), the lookup mergeMap['__proto__'] traverses the prototype chain and returns Object.prototype — a truthy non-function object. The subsequent call Object.prototype(...) throws TypeError: merge is not a function, crashing the Node.js process. This code path is triggered by all Axios HTTP method shortcuts (get, post, etc.), Axios._request(), and Axios.getUri(). Importantly, this is not prototype pollution — the crash occurs before any property assignment (GitHub Advisory, Fix Commit). Impact Successful exploitation results in a complete crash of any Node.js application that accepts user-controlled JSON, parses it with JSON.parse(), and passes the result to Axios configuration methods. The impact is limited to availability — there is no confidentiality or integrity impact. Applications relying on Axios for outbound HTTP requests (e.g., API gateways, backend services, microservices) would become entirely unresponsive, potentially causing cascading failures in dependent systems. The vulnerability has a broad downstream footprint, affecting numerous IBM enterprise products (including IBM Maximo Application Suite, IBM API Connect, IBM Cloud Pak for Business Automation, IBM watsonx Orchestrate, and others), Atlassian products, Splunk User Behavior Analytics, Red Hat packages, and HPE products (GitHub Advisory, IBM Advisory).
